title: Kipper and orange pâté on toast

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Kippers, oranges, butter, crème fraîche, horseradish sauce and bread are all traditional kitchen staples.

supermarket.reason: Kipper fillets, oranges and the rest are everyday items at Tesco at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: A kettle, a dish, a bowl and fork, and a toaster are ordinary kit, and pouring boiling water over kippers is beginner-level.

works.reason: Five minutes in boiling water is enough for kippers, the butter and crème fraîche loosen 300g of fish into a spreadable pâté for eight slices, and the salty fish needs only pepper.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is believable for flaking and boning the fish, peeling and slicing two oranges, mixing and toasting, and the 5-minute soak matches the cook time.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and the pepper are used, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears apart from boiling water.

seasonal_feel.reason: February oranges appear as zest in the pâté and as a full topping of two sliced oranges, a classic pairing with winter kippers that makes the citrus central.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oily fish on wholemeal toast with fresh orange is a filling, real-food snack a family would happily make again.
